issues.legal_issue: An unexplained injury to an accused, without circumstances establishing a reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt, does not establish a right of private defence permitting fatal force.
material_facts: The accused relied on an injury suffered by a co-accused, which the prosecution had not explained.

The evidence established a quarrel between the groups, but the circumstances did not establish that the accused faced a reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt requiring the use of fatal force.
issues.conclusion: The plea of private defence was not established.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 96–100 and 102 of the Indian Penal Code, private defence is preventive, not punitive, and the right to cause death is limited to circumstances giving reasonable grounds to apprehend death or grievous hurt; Section 99 limits force to what is necessary. The court applied Deo Narain v. State of U.P., Bishna Alias Bhiswadeb Mahato v. State of W.B., Surendra v. State of Maharashtra, Surendra Singh @ Bittu v. State of Uttaranchal, Siva Kumar v. State by Inspector of Police, and Hafiz v. State of U.P. An accused may rely on the circumstances of the case without examining defence witnesses, but the facts must make the plea probable.

predicates.criminal_appeal_with_private_defence_cla: The proceeding is a criminal appeal in which the accused claims to have acted in private defence.
predicates.accused_or_associate_injured: The accused or an associate suffered an injury during the incident.
predicates.evidence_of_reasonable_apprehension_of_d: The circumstances provide evidence that the accused reasonably apprehended death or grievous hurt.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal raises private defence and an accused or associate was injured, the claim is not established if the evidence does not show a reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt.

issues.legal_issue: A fatal single blow delivered during a sudden, unpremeditated quarrel, considered with the nature of the injury and all surrounding circumstances, may constitute culpable homicide not amounting to murder rather than murder.
material_facts: The accused was convicted of murder for causing the deceased’s fatal head injury during a dispute over construction of a wall.
The quarrel arose suddenly after construction had begun, following an ongoing dispute and an exchange of abuses; the evidence did not indicate premeditation.

Only one blow was inflicted. The witnesses differed about the weapon and the assailants’ roles, and the medical evidence was inconsistent about whether the head wound was incised or caused by a hard, blunt object.

A doctor testified that the injury could not have been caused by a sharp cutting weapon and could have resulted from a fall; another doctor described an incised wound. The possibility that the blow came from the blunt side of an axe could not be ruled out.
A co-accused had an unexplained injury, other accused were acquitted, and much of the prosecution account of their involvement was rejected.
issues.conclusion: The accused was not guilty of murder but was guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304, Part II of the Indian Penal Code; the appeal was allowed to that extent.
issues.legal_principle: Section 300, Exception 4, applies where the act occurs without premeditation, in a sudden fight, without undue advantage or cruel or unusual conduct. The court must assess intention and the nature of the offence holistically, considering the weapon, force, injury, suddenness of the quarrel, premeditation, and conduct. A blunt-force wound may resemble an incised wound, as explained in Shankaria v. State of Rajasthan. Under Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab, the elements of the relevant murder clause include intention to inflict the particular injury and that injury’s sufficiency to cause death in the ordinary course. The court also relied on Pappu v. State of Madhya Pradesh, Pulicherla Nagaraju @ Nagaraja Reddy v. State of A.P., and Rajinder v. State of Haryana in assessing the distinction between murder and culpable homicide; Section 304, Part II applies where the circumstances establish the lesser offence without the requisite basis for murder.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_murder_conviction and single_fatal_blow and sudden_quarrel_without_premeditation and not undue_advantage_or_cruel_conduct and surrounding_circumstances_do_not_establish_murder

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_murder_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal from a conviction for murder.
predicates.single_fatal_blow: The accused inflicted one blow that caused the victim’s fatal injury.
predicates.sudden_quarrel_without_premeditation: The fatal act occurred in a sudden quarrel and was not premeditated.
predicates.undue_advantage_or_cruel_conduct: The accused took undue advantage or acted cruelly or unusually during the incident.
predicates.surrounding_circumstances_do_not_establi: The evidence about the injury, weapon, intention, and incident as a whole does not establish murder.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a murder conviction, a single fatal blow in a sudden, unpremeditated quarrel may result in a reduced conviction when there was no undue advantage or cruel conduct and the surrounding circumstances do not establish murder.
